subject: INR
correct: INR 5–8 without bleeding: withhold 1–2 doses of warfarin and reduce the maintenance dose; vitamin K is for INR >8 (oral 1–5 mg) or for bleeding (BNF / BSH warfarin reversal)
source: https://bnf.nice.org.uk/treatment-summaries/oral-anticoagulants/ (BNF warfarin high INR table); consistent with site tools/algorithms/bruising.html

fixes.old: label:'INR 5–8 — withhold warfarin + oral vit K'
fixes.new: label:'INR 5–8 — withhold 1–2 doses of warfarin, reduce dose (vit K only if bleeding)'

note: The lab interpreter tells users to give oral vitamin K at INR 5–8 with no bleeding. BNF/BSH and the site's own bruising algorithm say to omit 1–2 doses and reduce the dose; vitamin K applies at INR >8 or with bleeding. High-risk drug.

subject: eosinophils
correct: Hypereosinophilia = eosinophils ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L on two occasions at least 4 weeks apart; >5.0 × 10⁹/L is 'severe' eosinophilia (BSH 2017)

fixes.old: {"chip":"Eosinophils >5.0 × 10⁹/L (","text":"No Eosinophils >5.0 × 10⁹/L (hypereosinophilia) on two readings 4 weeks apart
fixes.new: {"chip":"Eosinophils ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L (","text":"No Eosinophils ≥1.5 × 10⁹/L (hypereosinophilia) on two readings 4 weeks apart

note: Elsewhere the site (eosinophilia.html, leucocytosis.html, clinic guide) defines hypereosinophilia as ≥1.5. The red-flag entry gives the HES threshold as >5.0 while its own explanation says >1.5. The eosinophilia algorithm labels >5.0 as 'hypereosinophilia'; the same page already calls this band 'severe'.

subject: respiratory rate
correct: Acute severe asthma = ANY ONE of: PEF 33–50% best/predicted, RR ≥25/min, HR ≥110/min, inability to complete sentences (BTS/SIGN/NICE)

fixes.old: "text":"No Acute severe asthma: PEF 33-50% best/predicted + RR >25 + HR >110 + unable to complete sentences
fixes.new: "text":"No Acute severe asthma: any one of PEF 33–50% best/predicted, RR ≥25, HR ≥110 or unable to complete sentences

note: This red flag requires all four features ('+') and uses strict '>' thresholds. Every other page (asthma management, summaries, triage, AKT) uses 'any one of' with ≥25 and ≥110. As written, the flag under-triages an emergency.

subject: glucose
correct: DVLA (INF294, all groups): test within 2 h before driving and every 2 h; if 5.0 mmol/L or less, eat a snack first; do not drive if below 4.0 mmol/L or hypo symptoms; after a hypo wait 45 min after glucose returns to normal

fixes.old: do not drive if glucose <5 mmol/L; wait 45 min after hypo before driving
fixes.new: if glucose 5.0 mmol/L or less eat a snack first, and do not drive if below 4.0 mmol/L; wait 45 min after a hypo has been treated and glucose has recovered before driving
Must not drive if glucose <4.0 mmol/L (5.0 or less: eat a snack first — “five to drive”)

note: Only cases/type-2-diabetes.html gives a hard no-drive threshold of <5. Every other page (dvla.html, driving-diseases, insulin-type-2-diabetes, sca-addons-2, sca-cases56, sca-enrich) uses <4.0 no-drive and ≤5.0 snack. 'Five to drive' remains correct as advice.

subject: BMI
correct: NICE NG69: consider a bone mineral density scan after 2 years of underweight in adults, or 1 year in children and young people (earlier if bone pain or recurrent fractures)
source: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng69 (recs 1.3.18–1.3.19); the same file already quotes this rule in 6 places

fixes.old: DEXA if BMI below threshold for 1 year
fixes.new: DEXA after 2 years of underweight in adults (1 year in children and young people), or earlier if bone pain or recurrent fractures (NICE NG69)

fixes.old: DEXA bone density scan if amenorrhoea persists beyond 6 months
fixes.new: DEXA per NICE NG69 (after 2 years of underweight in adults, 1 year in children and young people, or earlier if bone pain or recurrent fractures)

note: Emma is 19, so the adult rule applies. The follow-up timeline (1 year) and the amenorrhoea row (>6 months) contradict the page's own repeated NG69 statement.

subject: BMI
correct: Semaglutide 1 mg weekly in T2DM: about 5–7% body weight loss (SUSTAIN trials, ~4.5–6.5 kg). 10–15% applies to the 2.4 mg obesity dose (STEP) in people without diabetes

fixes.old: Semaglutide (GLP-1 RA): 10–15% body weight loss; remission potential
fixes.new: Semaglutide (GLP-1 RA): about 5–7% body weight loss at diabetes doses (more with obesity-dose regimens); remission potential

fixes.old: BMI ≥35: GLP-1 RA preferred — 10–15% body weight loss with semaglutide
fixes.new: BMI ≥35: GLP-1 RA preferred — about 5–7% body weight loss with semaglutide 1 mg

fixes.old: BMI ≥35 — superior weight loss (10–15% body weight with semaglutide)
fixes.new: BMI ≥35 — superior weight loss (about 5–7% body weight with semaglutide 1 mg)

note: The case doses semaglutide at 0.25 mg rising to 1 mg (the diabetes dose) but quotes obesity-trial weight loss. assets/meds/type-2-diabetes.js says 5–15%, which is broadly acceptable.

subject: BMI
correct: Morbid (class III) obesity is BMI ≥40 kg/m²; BMI 36 is class II obesity
